chunks: Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ushnani al-Razi, the just one in Balkh, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Mihrawayh al-Quzwini narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Sulayman al-Farra', from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Divine unity is half of the religion, and invoke sustenance through charity.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Tawhid in Islam and how does charity affect sustenance?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this hadith underscores Tawhid not merely as a doctrinal belief but as the foundational half of the entire religious structure, linking metaphysical unity to practical ethics. The instruction to 'invite rizq through sadaqah reflects the Shia understanding of divine generosity, where material charity serves as a spiritual mechanism to unlock sustenance, echoing the concept of *barakah* in daily life.
